card.band: 20h. Regex-engine work is a big surface. Frontier agents get a literal prefilter and perhaps a lazy DFA, so they land well under 1.5x on average. A weaker model gets only memchr-style tricks, or breaks correctness.
card.cheat: Caching results by haystack. The hidden benchmarks use fresh patterns and haystacks and the timing runs are cold per process. Dependency vendoring is restricted to the shipped crates.
card.grading: A hard gate checks match spans and capture groups against the 1.7.3 oracle on thousands of generated pattern/haystack pairs. Then the median wall-clock speedup on hidden benchmarks is scored as 2^u-1 against our measured speedup.
card.reference: regex 1.9.0, a measured ~1.5x average on 242 benchmarks (single-source figure), with per-benchmark speedups far higher.
card.task: /app ships regex 1.7.3 as a history-less crate with a benchmark harness over a rebar-style set of patterns and haystacks. The agent speeds up search without changing semantics, through prefilters, inner literals, a lazy DFA, one-pass DFA captures or a bounded backtracker. The public API is unchanged.
card.title: Rust regex 1.7 to 1.9 search speedup

history: Reference median speedup is about 1.13-1.17x, below the 1.3x pass bar, so a median-based score has almost no headroom; Differential oracle disagrees between 1.7.3 and 1.9.0 on nested empty-loop patterns: 119 span mismatches and 3936 span-or-capture mismatches of 32000 pairs (564 patterns); needs fil
source_notes: q:"Across 242 benchmarks, regex 1.9 is on average 1.5 times faster than regex 1.7.3 for search times." (read via WebFetch summariser; single-source for the 1.5x, verify against page). Levers: literal prefilters incl. inner literals (memchr/memmem, Teddy, aho-corasick), lazy DFA, one-pass DFA for captures, bounded backtracker, minimal-UTF8 NFA, meta-engine strategy selection. Changelog 1.9.0 lists PERF #68 one-pass DFA, #510 inner literals. Independent correctness gate easy (match spans vs old version). rebar harness is Unlicense (github.com/BurntSushi/rebar).
source_version: regex 1.7.3 (rebar entry rust/regexold) -> regex 1.9.0 (2023-07-05; blog tables measured 1.8.4)

blockers: Reference median speedup is about 1.13-1.17x, below the 1.3x pass bar, so a median-based score has almost no headroom
Differential oracle disagrees between 1.7.3 and 1.9.0 on nested empty-loop patterns: 119 span mismatches and 3936 span-or-capture mismatches of 32000 pairs (564 patterns); needs filtering
Timing noise is high: only 27% of same-engine benchmark pairs agree within 10% between two runs, though aggregate medians agree
rebar measures a warm in-process loop, not cold processes as the seed specifies; cold-process timing not tested
Speedups are concentrated in a few outlier benchmarks, so the score would depend on which hidden benchmarks are chosen
spike.commands_log: git clone BurntSushi/rebar; cargo build --release; copied engines/rust/regex-old to regex-new pinned regex =1.9.0; added rust/regexnew to engine lists; rebar measure -e 'rust/regex(old|new)$' -M compile --max-time 200ms --max-warmup-time 80ms x3; /work/diff random generator built per pinned version, outputs compared
spike.headroom_note: Median 1.9.0 speedup over 1.7.3 is about 1.13-1.17x across 3 runs (1.129, 1.129, 1.169), below the 1.3x pass bar. Geomean about 2.0-2.3x is inflated by outliers up to ~1e5x. 45-61 of ~240 benchmarks are slower in 1.9.0.
spike.notes: Both versions built. 236-251 comparable benchmarks per run, compile excluded. Median speedup 1.129, 1.129, 1.169; geomean 1.96, 2.12, 2.29. Differential: 4000 random patterns x 8 haystacks, 3936 of 32000 lines differ (119 in spans), all nested empty-repeat patterns. Memchr-prefilter patch and cold-process timing not run. Notes in /work/SPIKE.md.

facts.claim: regex 1.9.0 released 2023-07-05 with a changelog entry
1.9.0 PERF #68: one-pass DFA engine for faster capture group matching
1.9.0 PERF #510: inner literals accelerate searches (e.g. \w+@\w+ scans for @)
regex 1.9 internals were largely rewritten; main expected change is faster search
Internals post describes a lazy DFA built during search and a one-pass DFA faster than PikeVM/backtracker
regex 1.9 is on average 1.5x faster than 1.7.3 across 242 benchmarks
Same 1.5x / 242-benchmark figure in changelog or internals post
regex repository licence is MIT OR Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE present; page shows no SPDX expression)
rebar benchmark harness is Unlicense and is a cross-engine regex benchmark suite with patterns and haystacks
Frontier agents land well under 1.5x on this task

full_card.band: 20h tier proposed. Frontier likely reaches part of the inner-literal and one-pass levers; full 1.9-scope finish not evidenced. No dated public agent evidence.
full_card.build_cost: About 3-5 days: crate snapshot, rebar harness wiring, differential generator, cold-process timing protocol, and a measured reference speedup.
full_card.deliverable: Faster search in the regex 1.7.3 crate with unchanged public API and identical match spans and capture groups.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Cold per-process timing; hidden patterns and haystacks fresh; no haystack-result caching; vendoring limited to shipped crates; no cargo registry copy of regex-automata 0.3 or 1.9 in the image; no network at run time.
full_card.grading_surface: Hard gate: match spans and captures vs 1.7.3 on thousands of generated pattern/haystack pairs. Score: median cold-process wall-clock speedup on hidden rebar-style benchmarks, mapped to 2^u-1.
full_card.local_fit: Rust toolchain must be in the image and build offline with shipped crates only; CPU-only, fits 8 cores / 16 GB; no gVisor-incompatible features expected.
full_card.lookup: partial: 1.9 design is public in the release notes, blog and internals post; code is in a later public release not installable offline and must be excluded from /app.
full_card.provenance: rust-lang/regex 1.7.3 tag (commit 9582040) to 1.9.0 release (2023-07-05); MIT OR Apache-2.0; rebar harness Unlicense.
full_card.reference: regex 1.9.0 (public, permissive). Claimed ~1.5x average over 242 benchmarks is UNVERIFIED; must be measured in the spike.
full_card.ships: History-less regex 1.7.3 crate, rebar-style benchmark harness with a visible subset of patterns and haystacks, and the 1.7.3 oracle for differential checks.
full_card.similarity: l0 max 0.207 (S-op-010); no near-duplicate seen. Subject is a regex engine, which is on the CROWDED list, but deliverable is optimisation of an existing engine graded against an upstream speedup, so it is not the same task.

Band.why: Plausible frontier difficulty, but no dated public evidence, so capped at 3.

Build.why: Estimated 3-5 days for snapshot, harness, differential gate and measured reference.

Fit.why: CPU-only and within limits; needs a Rust toolchain and offline vendoring.

Hor.why: Several levers over a large engine; sustained work of a multi-hour scale.

Lic.why: MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the crate and Unlicense for rebar, both confirmed.

Multi.why: Prefilters, inner literals, one-pass DFA, backtracker and lazy DFA are separate buckets by benchmark family.

Nov.why: Regex engines are a CROWDED subject, but the optimisation deliverable differs; max l0 neighbour 0.207.

Real.why: Real crate with confirmed 1.7.3 tag and 1.9.0 changelog; the 1.5x claim is unverified.

Ref.why: 1.9.0 is a complete permissive public release, but its speedup is unmeasured and the 1.5x/242 figure is not found in any source.

Seal.why: 1.9.0 is public; the snapshot must exclude it and the cargo registry, and recall is only partial at design level.

Surf.why: Executable oracle (1.7.3 shipped) with an unlimited generator plus a rebar benchmark set.

spike_plan.kill_if: The median 1.9.0 speedup is at most 1.1x (too little headroom), or the differential check shows mismatches between versions (oracle unusable), or variance exceeds about 25% (no stable score).
spike_plan.pass_if: 1.9.0 median speedup over 1.7.3 is at least 1.3x on the rebar set, run-to-run variance is within about 10%, and the differential generator shows zero span or capture mismatches between 1.7.3 and 1.9.0.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, fetch regex 1.7.3 and 1.9.0 from crates.io and build both with a Rust toolchain.
Clone BurntSushi/rebar, build it, and run its regex benchmark set against both versions in cold processes, 3 runs each.
Compute per-benchmark speedups (1.7.3 time / 1.9.0 time), then the median and geometric mean across benchmarks, and count how many benchmarks there are (to test the 242 and 1.5x claims).
Run a differential generator (several thousand random pattern/haystack pairs) comparing match spans and capture groups between 1.7.3 and 1.9.0; record any mismatches.
Measure a minimal literal-prefilter (memchr) patch on 1.7.3 to see how much headroom the cheap lever gives.
Check run-to-run variance of the medians; if above roughly 10%, note the noise floor for grading.

v1.summary: The seed is a real, permissively licensed regex 1.7.3 to 1.9.0 optimisation with a confirmed 1.9.0 changelog (PERF #68 one-pass DFA, PERF #510 inner literals) and a confirmed Unlicense rebar harness, but the headline 1.5x average over 242 benchmarks is not found in any source checked and must be measured. Viability is unconfirmed pending a 60-minute spike that measures the reference speedup on the rebar set, checks differential correctness between 1.7.3 and 1.9.0, and confirms run-to-run stability.

v2.note: The upstream perf series is real and permissively licensed, and the span/capture differential gate is generator-backed. The 1.5x/242-benchmark figure is unverified. The card overstates the levers: 1.7.3 already has a lazy DFA and memchr/aho-corasick/Teddy prefilters, so the real headroom is inner literals, the one-pass DFA, reverse-suffix/inner strategies and meta-engine selection. The median speedup could therefore be small; the spike must measure it under gVisor timing. 1.9 changed some semantics (e.g. empty matches in the bytes API), so the gate must use only 1.7.3-identical behaviour. The image must not contain regex-automata 0.3 or regex 1.9 in ~/.cargo. The regex subject is crowded, but the optimisation deliverable differs.
